extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, physicians, chemists, astronomers, and antiquarians (readers/contributors to Philosophical Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or producing short empirical reports (medical case histories, chemical/physical experiments, archaeological notes, and astronomical observations) as published in a 17th-century scientific journal. Emphasis is on precise chronology, instrument/method description, specimen/measurement details, and interpretive caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical case report: patient demographics and chronology
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the patient's identifying details (age, approximate dates) and a clear chronological narrative of the illness (dates of onset, admissions, relapses, and discharge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Konig case lists age (~25), exact dates (e.g., spring 1678, 3rd January 1680, admissions on specific days), and timelines of treatments and outcomes; a good report should provide comparable temporal anchors so readers can follow progression and correlate treatments with effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical case report: detailed signs, symptoms, and objective observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Record specific clinical signs and symptoms (locations and character of pain, eruptions, pulse character, appetite, vomiting) and objective findings (urine colour/volume, presence and character of expelled calculi, abdominal sounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The case includes descriptions such as vesicular eruption of a hand's breadth, irregular pulse, suppression of urine, green/blue urine, quantities (e.g., 4 oz. of green urine drawn off), and sounds like 'clashing of stones' on palpation. Reports should quantify and richly describe such phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical case report: interventions with dosages and administration details
rubrics_metrics.description: List therapies, their forms, dosages, frequencies, routes (e.g., venesection, clysters, baths, mercurial salivation, spirit of nitre, quicksilver amounts), and procedural particulars (catheter use, holding mouth closed after swallowing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrative specifies e.g., '4 oz. of quicksilver' given on a date, '6 oz. of thick green urine drawn off by the catheter', polychrest salt regimen (6 oz. every quarter hour until 3 pints). Such precision enables assessment of causality and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical case report: measurements and specimen description
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide weights, sizes, colours, textures, and chemical behaviour of pathological specimens (stones/calculi, faeces, urine sediments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author records calculi varying from pea-size to 2 drachms, colours (white, red, grey), surfaces (rough, smooth), internal structure, and notes dissolution behaviour in acids. Good reports preserve or describe specimens and their chemical reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical case report: outcome, follow-up, and open questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe patient outcome and recovery status, frequency of follow-up measurements, and explicitly state puzzling phenomena and questions for further inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Konig reports recovery level (walking about, making 3–5 oz. clear urine daily), continuing symptoms, and poses explicit questions (how could urine reach the stomach? why colour changes?). Including such questions guides future investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutic caution / clinical inference
rubrics_metrics.description: When interpreting interventions, advise prudence about commonly used practices—especially repelling/suppressing cutaneous affections—where suppression may cause deeper pathology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor's comment: 'how cautious practitioners should be in repelling or suppressing some kinds of cutaneous affections' functions as a practice-guideline warning. Reports should note potential iatrogenic risks and reasoning behind treatment choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental description: apparatus and construction details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide concrete construction specifications for experimental apparatus (materials, dimensions, notches/holes, linings, grate placement) so others can reproduce the apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bolognese-stone furnace is specified (cylindrical iron or copper plates ~7 in. diameter and ~7 in. high; lute lining to make ~6 in. hollow; 4 notches 2-1/2 in. high etc.). Supply such granular details for reproducibility and control of heating conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental procedure: material preparation and stepwise method
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe stepwise preparation (powdering, immersion in solvent, layering on charcoal, capping, burning to completion), timing and sequence, and post-treatment handling (removing crust, wrapping, storage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For preparing the stone: beat into powder, dip stones in strong aquavitae, roll in powder, lay on charcoal bed, cover and burn until coals consumed, remove crust, wrap in silk, keep in closed box. Such procedural exactness affects product quality and should be recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental control of key variables (heat, exposure, storage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report and control critical variables (degree of heat, duration, exposure to sun/air, storage conditions) and note effects of deviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author warns that 'if too great [heat], it will destroy the quality; if too little, it will not raise it' and that the stone 'retains not its light long, nor its virtue above 5 or 6 years.' Indicate sensitivity to these variables and document handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental observation and reporting of phenomena (phosphorus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe observed behaviours qualitatively and quantitatively (ignition in glass bulb, flame behaviour, residues, effects in vacuo, mass changes, solubility, corrosivity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slare's experiments report: sealed glass-ball ignition on warming, chimney accumulation of yellow sulphur, burning without explosion, leaving 'red tenacious matter', dissolving iron, greater apparent mass after exposure. Record such observations, mass/weight changes, and residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental testing under variant conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically test a substance under different environments (open air, vacuo, immersion in various liquids, bellows-forced air) and report contrasting behaviours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slare tested the shining matter in air, in vacuo with an air-pump (increased light), on re-admission of air (dulled), with bellows (extinguished), and by plunging into different liquids (extinguished). Experimental reports should include these comparative conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopic / observational natural-history reporting (Leeuwenhoek)
rubrics_metrics.description: State sample sources, preparation methods, what was examined, comparative size references (e.g., fractions of a blood globule), morphological description (globules, threads), mobility, and include drawings when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leeuwenhoek reports examinations of hair, excrements, and urine, gives relative sizes ('one sixth, one thirty-sixth of a blood globule'), and uses drawings to clarify bristle structure. Such detail supports reproducibility and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archaeological/antiquarian reporting: typology and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify artifacts by temper/composition/colour/decoration and relate findspots, kiln evidence, and manufacturing traces to infer production locales and techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dr. Lister distinguishes three urn tempers (bluish grey with coarse sand; bluish with fine sand/mica; red fine clay), notes findspots near Roman road and kilns, and infers glazing was done before firing. Reports should combine typology with contextual field evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archaeological comparative reasoning and material analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare artifact techniques and materials with modern or classical descriptions, cite literary authorities where relevant, and use material evidence (slag, cinders, furnace ruins) to support arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lister compares ancient glazing with modern lead glazes, cites Pliny on bitumen, and points to slag and kilns to locate workshops. Include such comparative discussion and cite sources to strengthen provenance claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomical observation reporting: precise timing and positional detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Report times to the second (h m s), specify instrument (e.g., 16-foot tube), give measured quantities (moon diameter in seconds/arc), and describe positions of immersion/emergence relative to lunar features (spots, palus, insula).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flamsteed records immersion at '3 5 42', moon diameter '6595 = 32' 54"', and places of immersion relative to 'Palus Maraeotis' and specific spots. Precise temporal and positional data are essential for reproducibility and later analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit reporting of anomalies and interpretive humility
rubrics_metrics.description: When observations are puzzling or contradictory (e.g., catheter stuck but urine later voided spontaneously; shining matter increasing light in vacuo), explicitly report anomalies and avoid premature definitive explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Konig case poses many questions without definitive answers; Slare notes surprising mass increase on exposure. Such candid reporting of anomalies guides further enquiry and signals limits of current understanding.
